title:	fix: project root detection, force-rescan plan wipe, and auto-cluster triage
state:	OPEN

## Summary

Three fixes discovered while running desloppify on a real project:

- **fix: derive project root from state_file path in do_import_run follow-up scan** — `--scan-after-import` was writing state to `.desloppify/subagents/runs/<stamp>/results/.desloppify/` instead of the project root's `.desloppify/`. Root cause: `_runtime_project_root()` returned the wrong path. Fix: use `Path(state_file).parent.parent` which is always correct.

- **fix: preserve plan_start_scores during force-rescan to protect manual clusters** — `--force-rescan` was wiping manual cluster items while keeping cluster names. Root cause: `_reset_cycle_for_force_rescan()` cleared `plan_start_scores`, making `is_mid_cycle()` return False, which triggered full cluster regeneration and issue ID reconciliation that superseded all old IDs. Fix: don't clear `plan_start_scores` during force-rescan.

- **feat: require explicit triage decisions for auto-clusters** — Auto-clusters (auto/unused, auto/security, etc.) entered the execution queue but were invisible to triage ("silence means leave in backlog"). Now the triage prompt requires an explicit decision (promote/skip/break_up) for each auto-cluster, with a structured `auto_cluster_decisions` field in the triage output schema.

## Test plan

- [x] All 5380 existing tests pass
- [ ] Run `desloppify review --import-run <dir> --scan-after-import` and verify state writes to correct location
- [ ] Run `desloppify scan --force-rescan` with manual clusters and verify they survive
- [ ] Run triage and verify auto-clusters appear with "decision required" prompt

title:	fix(engine): prevent workflow::create-plan re-injection after resolution
state:	OPEN
author:	cdunda-perchwell
labels:	
assignees:

milestone:

url:	https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify/pull/435
additions:	94
deletions:	28
auto-merge:	disabled
--
## Summary

`sync_create_plan_needed()` had no sentinel to prevent re-injection after `workflow::create-plan` was resolved. Unlike `sync_communicate_score_needed()` which uses `previous_plan_start_scores`, the create-plan sync only checked whether objective backlog existed — which is always true mid-cycle. After resolving the item, `_reconcile_if_queue_drained()` calls `reconcile_plan()` which calls `sync_create_plan_needed()` again, and re-injects it.

## Fix

Add `create_plan_resolved_this_cycle` sentinel mirroring the existing `previous_plan_start_scores` pattern:

- Set when `workflow::create-plan` is injected
- Cleared at the same cycle boundaries (force-rescan, score seeding, queue drain, trusted review import)
- Checked in `sync_create_plan_needed()` to prevent re-injection within the same cycle

## Files changed

- `desloppify/engine/_plan/sync/workflow.py` — added sentinel check/set in `sync_create_plan_needed()`, added `clear_create_plan_sentinel()`, updated `__all__`
- `desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py` — wire `clear_create_plan_sentinel()` at 3 cycle-boundary sites
- `desloppify/app/commands/review/importing/plan_sync.py` — wire `clear_create_plan_sentinel()` at trusted import site

## Testing

- 273 PRR tests pass
- 532 plan tests pass
- 5381 broader tests pass (8 pre-existing failures in test_scoring.py from missing imports, unrelated)

Fixes #434

60→+**Don't be lazy.** Do large refactors and small detailed fixes with equal energy. If it takes touching 20 files, touch 20 files. If it's a one-line change, make it. No task is too big or too small — fix things properly, not minimally.
    61→+
    62→+## 2. The Workflow
    63→+
    64→+Three phases, repeated as a cycle.
    65→+
    66→+### Phase 1: Scan and review — understand the codebase
    67→+
    68→+```bash
    69→+desloppify scan --path .       # analyse the codebase
    70→+desloppify status              # check scores — are we at target?
    71→+```
    72→+
    73→+The scan will tell you if subjective dimensions need review. Follow its instructions. To trigger a review manually:
    74→+```bash
    75→+desloppify review --prepare    # then follow your runner's review workflow
    76→+```
    77→+
    78→+### Phase 2: Plan — decide what to work on
    79→+
    80→+After reviews, triage stages and plan creation appear in the execution queue surfaced by `next`. Complete them in order — `next` tells you what each stage expects in the `--report`:
    81→+```bash
    82→+desloppify next                                        # shows the next execution workflow step
    83→+desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "themes and root causes..."
    84→+desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "comparison against completed work..."
    85→+desloppify plan triage --stage organize --report "summary of priorities..."
    86→+desloppify plan triage --complete --strategy "execution plan..."
    87→+```
    88→+
    89→+For automated triage: `desloppify plan triage --run-stages --runner codex` (Codex) or `--runner claude` (Claude). Options: `--only-stages`, `--dry-run`, `--stage-timeout-seconds`.
    90→+
    91→+Then shape the queue. **The plan shapes everything `next` gives you** — `next` is the execution queue, not the full backlog. Don't skip this step.
    92→+
    93→+```bash
    94→+desloppify plan                          # see the living plan details
    95→+desloppify plan queue                    # compact execution queue view
    96→+desloppify plan reorder <pat> top        # reorder — what unblocks the most?
    97→+desloppify plan cluster create <name>    # group related issues to batch-fix
    98→+desloppify plan focus <cluster>          # scope next to one cluster
    99→+desloppify plan skip <pat>              # defer — hide from next
   100→+```
   101→+
   102→+### Phase 3: Execute — grind the queue to completion
   103→+
   104→+Trust the plan and execute. Don't rescan mid-queue — finish the queue first.
   105→+
   106→+**Branch first.** Create a dedicated branch — never commit health work directly to main:
   107→+```bash
   108→+git checkout -b desloppify/code-health    # or desloppify/<focus-area>
   109→+desloppify config set commit_pr 42        # link a PR for auto-updated descriptions
   110→+```
   111→+
   112→+**The loop:**
   113→+```bash
   114→+# 1. Get the next item from the execution queue
   115→+desloppify next
   116→+
   117→+# 2. Fix the issue in code
   118→+
   119→+# 3. Resolve it (next shows the exact command including required attestation)
   120→+
   121→+# 4. When you have a logical batch, commit and record
   122→+git add <files> && git commit -m "desloppify: fix 3 deferred_import findings"
   123→+desloppify plan commit-log record      # moves findings uncommitted → committed, updates PR
   124→+
   125→+# 5. Push periodically
   126→+git push -u origin desloppify/code-health
   127→+
   128→+# 6. Repeat until the queue is empty
   129→+```
   130→+
   131→+Score may temporarily drop after fixes — cascade effects are normal, keep going.
   132→+If `next` suggests an auto-fixer, run `desloppify autofix <fixer> --dry-run` to preview, then apply.
   133→+
   134→+**When the queue is clear, go back to Phase 1.** New issues will surface, cascades will have resolved, priorities will have shifted. This is the cycle.
   135→+
   136→+## 3. Reference
   137→+
   138→+### Key concepts
   139→+
   140→+- **Tiers**: T1 auto-fix → T2 quick manual → T3 judgment call → T4 major refactor.
   141→+- **Auto-clusters**: related findings are auto-grouped in `next`. Drill in with `next --cluster <name>`.
   142→+- **Zones**: production/script (scored), test/config/generated/vendor (not scored). Fix with `zone set`.
   143→+- **Wontfix cost**: widens the lenient↔strict gap. Challenge past decisions when the gap grows.
   144→+
   145→+### Scoring
   146→+
   147→+Overall score = **25% mechanical** + **75% subjective**.
   148→+
   149→+- **Mechanical (25%)**: auto-detected issues — duplication, dead code, smells, unused imports, security. Fixed by changing code and rescanning.
   150→+- **Subjective (75%)**: design quality review — naming, error handling, abstractions, clarity. Starts at **0%** until reviewed. The scan will prompt you when a review is needed.
   151→+- **Strict score** is the north star: wontfix items count as open. The gap between overall and strict is your wontfix debt.
   152→+- **Score types**: overall (lenient), strict (wontfix counts), objective (mechanical only), verified (confirmed fixes only).
   153→+
   154→+### Reviews
   155→+
   156→+Four paths to get subjective scores:
   157→+
   158→+- **Local runner (Codex)**: `desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import` — automated end-to-end.
   159→+- **Local runner (Claude)**: `desloppify review --prepare` → launch parallel subagents → `desloppify review --import merged.json` — see skill doc overlay for details.
   160→+- **Cloud/external**: `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude` → follow session template → `--external-submit`.
   161→+- **Manual path**: `desloppify review --prepare` → review per dimension → `desloppify review --import file.json`.
   162→+
   163→+- Import first, fix after — import creates tracked state entries for correlation.
   164→+- Target-matching scores trigger auto-reset to prevent gaming. Use the blind-review workflow described in your agent overlay doc (e.g. `docs/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/HERMES.md`).
   165→+- Even moderate scores (60-80) dramatically improve overall health.
   166→+- Stale dimensions auto-surface in `next` — just follow the queue.
   167→+
   168→+**Integrity rules:** Score from evidence only — no prior chat context, score history, or target-threshold anchoring. When evidence is mixed, score lower and explain uncertainty. Assess every requested dimension; never drop one.
   169→+
   170→+#### Review output format
   171→+
   172→+Return machine-readable JSON for review imports. For `--external-submit`, include `session` from the generated template:
   173→+
   174→+```json
   175→+{
   176→+  "session": {
   177→+    "id": "<session_id_from_template>",
   178→+    "token": "<session_token_from_template>"
   179→+  },
   180→+  "assessments": {
   181→+    "<dimension_from_query>": 0
   182→+  },
   183→+  "findings": [
   184→+    {
   185→+      "dimension": "<dimension_from_query>",
   186→+      "identifier": "short_id",
   187→+      "summary": "one-line defect summary",
   188→+      "related_files": ["relative/path/to/file.py"],
   189→+      "evidence": ["specific code observation"],
   190→+      "suggestion": "concrete fix recommendation",
   191→+      "confidence": "high|medium|low"
   192→+    }
   193→+  ]
   194→+}
   195→+```
   196→+
   197→+`findings` MUST match `query.system_prompt` exactly (including `related_files`, `evidence`, and `suggestion`). Use `"findings": []` when no defects found. Import is fail-closed: invalid findings abort unless `--allow-partial` is passed. Assessment scores are auto-applied from trusted internal or cloud session imports. Legacy `--attested-external` remains supported.
   198→+
   199→+#### Import paths
   200→+
   201→+- Robust session flow (recommended): `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude` → use generated prompt/template → run printed `--external-submit` command.
   202→+- Durable scored import (legacy): `desloppify review --import findings.json --attested-external --attest "I validated this review was completed without awareness of overall score and is unbiased."`
   203→+- Findings-only fallback: `desloppify review --import findings.json`
   204→+
   205→+#### Reviewer agent prompt
   206→+
   207→+Runners that support agent definitions (Cursor, Copilot, Gemini) can create a dedicated reviewer agent. Use this system prompt:
   208→+
   209→+```
   210→+You are a code quality reviewer. You will be given a codebase path, a set of
   211→+dimensions to score, and what each dimension means. Read the code, score each
   212→+dimension 0-100 from evidence only, and return JSON in the required format.
   213→+Do not anchor to target thresholds. When evidence is mixed, score lower and
   214→+explain uncertainty.
   215→+```
   216→+
   217→+See your editor's overlay section below for the agent config format.
   218→+
   219→+### Plan commands
   220→+
   221→+```bash
   222→+desloppify plan reorder <cluster> top       # move all cluster members at once
   223→+desloppify plan reorder <a> <b> top        # mix clusters + findings in one reorder
   224→+desloppify plan reorder <pat> before -t X  # position relative to another item/cluster
   225→+desloppify plan cluster reorder a,b top    # reorder multiple clusters as one block
   226→+desloppify plan resolve <pat>              # mark complete
   227→+desloppify plan reopen <pat>               # reopen
   228→+desloppify backlog                          # broader non-execution backlog
   229→+```
   230→+
   231→+### Commit tracking
   232→+
   233→+```bash
   234→+desloppify plan commit-log                      # see uncommitted + committed status
   235→+desloppify plan commit-log record               # record HEAD commit, update PR description
   236→+desloppify plan commit-log record --note "why"  # with rationale
   237→+desloppify plan commit-log record --only "smells::*"  # record specific findings only
   238→+desloppify plan commit-log history              # show commit records
   239→+desloppify plan commit-log pr                   # preview PR body markdown
   240→+desloppify config set commit_tracking_enabled false  # disable guidance
   241→+```
   242→+
   243→+After resolving findings as `fixed`, the tool shows uncommitted work, committed history, and a suggested commit message. After committing externally, run `record` to move findings from uncommitted to committed and auto-update the linked PR description.
   244→+
   245→+### Quick reference
   246→+
   247→+```bash
   248→+desloppify next --count 5                         # top 5 execution items
   249→+desloppify next --cluster <name>                  # drill into a cluster
   250→+desloppify backlog --count 5                      # top 5 backlog items outside execution
   251→+desloppify show <pattern>                         # filter by file/detector/ID
   252→+desloppify show --status open                     # all open findings
   253→+desloppify plan skip --permanent "<id>" --note "reason" --attest "..." # accept debt
   254→+desloppify exclude <path>                         # exclude a directory from scanning
   255→+desloppify config show                            # show all config including excludes
   256→+desloppify scan --path . --reset-subjective       # reset subjective baseline to 0
   257→+```
   258→+
   259→+## 4. Fix Tool Issues Upstream
   260→+
   261→+When desloppify itself appears wrong or inconsistent — a bug, a bad detection, a crash, confusing output — **fix it and open a PR**. If you can't confidently fix it, file an issue instead.
   262→+
   263→+### Fix and PR (preferred)
   264→+
   265→+Clone the tool repo to a temp directory, make the fix there, and verify it works against the project you're scanning before pushing.
   266→+
   267→+```bash
   268→+git clone https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify.git /tmp/desloppify-fix
   269→+cd /tmp/desloppify-fix
   270→+git checkout -b fix/<short-description>
   271→+```
   272→+
   273→+Make your changes, then run the test suite and verify the fix against the original project:
   274→+
   275→+```bash
   276→+python -m pytest desloppify/tests/ -q
   277→+python -m desloppify scan --path <project-root>   # the project you were scanning
   278→+```
   279→+
   280→+Once it looks good, push and open a PR:
   281→+
   282→+```bash
   283→+git add <files> && git commit -m "fix: <what and why>"
   284→+git push -u origin fix/<short-description>
   285→+gh pr create --title "fix: <short description>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
   286→+## Problem
   287→+<what went wrong — include the command and output>
   288→+
   289→+## Fix
   290→+<what you changed and why>
   291→+EOF
   292→+)"
   293→+```
   294→+
   295→+Clean up after: `rm -rf /tmp/desloppify-fix`
   296→+
   297→+### File an issue (fallback)
   298→+
   299→+If the fix is unclear or the change needs discussion, open an issue at `https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify/issues` with a minimal repro: command, path, expected output, actual output.
   300→+
   301→+## Prerequisite
   302→+
   303→+`command -v desloppify >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "desloppify: installed" || echo "NOT INSTALLED — run: pip install --upgrade git+https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify.git"`
   304→+
   305→+<!-- desloppify-end -->
   306→+
   307→+## Codex Overlay
   308→+
   309→+This is the canonical Codex overlay used by the README install command.
   310→+
   311→+1. Prefer first-class batch runs: `desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import`.
   312→+2. The command writes immutable packet snapshots under `.desloppify/review_packets/holistic_packet_*.json`; use those for reproducible retries.
   313→+3. Keep reviewer input scoped to the immutable packet and the source files named in each batch.
   314→+4. If a batch fails, retry only that slice with `desloppify review --run-batches --packet <packet.json> --only-batches <idxs>`.
   315→+5. Manual override is safety-scoped: you cannot combine it with `--allow-partial`, and provisional manual scores expire on the next `scan` unless replaced by trusted internal or attested-external imports.
   316→+
   317→+### Triage workflow
   318→+
   319→+Prefer automated triage: `desloppify plan triage --run-stages --runner codex`
   320→+
   321→+Options: `--only-stages observe,reflect` (subset), `--dry-run` (prompts only), `--stage-timeout-seconds N` (per-stage).
   322→+
   323→+Run artifacts go to `.desloppify/triage_runs/<timestamp>/` — each run gets its own directory with `run.log` (live timestamped events), `run_summary.json`, per-stage `prompts/`, `output/`, and `logs/`. Check `run.log` to diagnose stalls or failures. Re-running resumes from the last confirmed stage.
   324→+
   325→+If automated triage stalls, check `run.log` for the last event, then use `desloppify plan triage --stage-prompt <stage>` to get the full prompt with gate rules.
   326→+
   327→+<!-- desloppify-overlay: codex -->
   328→+<!-- desloppify-end -->

title:	Fix unused import detection for JS/TS (binding-aware, per-symbol issues)
state:	OPEN
author:	MacHatter1
labels:	
assignees:	
reviewers:	
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	433
url:	https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify/pull/433
additions:	632

--
Closes #430.

This replaces module-path/basename matching with binding-aware unused import detection for JavaScript/JSX and TypeScript/TSX:
- Parses `import_statement` bindings (default, named, aliased, namespace).
- Builds a reference set from AST identifiers outside import declarations (includes JSX tags and TS type identifiers).
- Flags only truly-unused imported local bindings.
- Emits one issue per unused symbol with name format `unused_import::<line>::<symbol>`.
- Keeps side-effect imports (`import "x"`) unflagged.
- Handles multiline imports.

Robustness:
- Some real OSS fixtures contained stray NUL bytes which can cause tree-sitter parse truncation and false positives; we replace NUL with space and re-parse, and skip files that still parse with errors.

Tests:
- Added/extended tests for JS/JSX + TS/TSX (default/named/alias/namespace, partial unused, side-effect imports, issue id format, default-value usages, TS type-only imports, NUL-byte regression).

Evidence:
- Benchmarked on create-react-app, docusaurus, gatsby (scanning up to 1200 files per repo). New detector substantially reduces false positives, and side-effect-import false positives drop to 0 across runs.
---DIFF---

index f0689991..0064064e 100644
--- a/desloppify/languages/_framework/treesitter/analysis/unused_imports.py
+++ b/desloppify/languages/_framework/treesitter/analysis/unused_imports.py
@@ -19,6 +19,34 @@
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
+_ECMASCRIPT_IMPORT_NODE_TYPE = "import_statement"
+
+# Identifier-ish nodes that represent a reference to a binding in JavaScript/TypeScript.
+# JSX tag names are typically represented as `identifier` in tree-sitter-javascript/tsx,
+# but we include `jsx_identifier` as well for compatibility with grammar variants.
+_ECMASCRIPT_REFERENCE_NODE_TYPES = frozenset({
+    "identifier",
+    "jsx_identifier",
+    "type_identifier",
+    "shorthand_property_identifier",
+})
+
+_ECMASCRIPT_ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN_NODE_TYPES = frozenset({
+    "assignment_pattern",
+    "object_assignment_pattern",
+    "array_assignment_pattern",
+})
+
+_ECMASCRIPT_DECLARATION_NAME_NODE_TYPES = frozenset({
+    # JS
+    "function_declaration",
+    "class_declaration",
+    # TS/TSX
+    "type_alias_declaration",
+    "interface_declaration",
+    "enum_declaration",
+})
+
 
 def detect_unused_imports(
     file_list: list[str],
@@ -37,6 +65,11 @@ def detect_unused_imports(
         logger.debug("tree-sitter init failed: %s", exc)
         return []
 
+    # JavaScript/JSX: extract imported *local bindings* and check whether each
+    # binding is referenced in the file body. This avoids module-path heuristics.
+    if spec.grammar in ("javascript", "tsx"):
+        return _detect_unused_imports_ecmascript(file_list, spec, parser, language)
+
     query = _make_query(language, spec.import_query)
     entries: list[dict] = []
 
@@ -89,6 +122,267 @@ def detect_unused_imports(
     return entries
 
 
+def _detect_unused_imports_ecmascript(
+    file_list: list[str],
+    spec: TreeSitterLangSpec,
+    parser,
+    language,
+) -> list[dict]:
+    """Binding-aware unused import detection for JavaScript/TypeScript (JSX/TSX).
+
+    Emits one entry per unused imported local binding:
+    {file, line, name, symbol}
+
+    Side-effect-only imports (e.g. `import "x"`) are ignored.
+    """
+    query = _make_query(language, f"({_ECMASCRIPT_IMPORT_NODE_TYPE}) @import")
+    entries: list[dict] = []
+
+    for filepath in file_list:
+        cached = get_or_parse_tree(filepath, parser, spec.grammar)
+        if cached is None:
+            continue
+        source, tree = cached
+
+        # Some real-world repos contain stray NUL bytes (e.g. broken fixtures).
+        # Tree-sitter can treat these as parse-stopping errors, leading to false
+        # positives due to missing references. Replace NUL with space (same length)
+        # and re-parse for analysis.
+        if b"\x00" in source:
+            source = source.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
+            tree = parser.parse(source)
+
+        # If the parse is still errorful, be conservative and skip this file to
+        # avoid false positives from incomplete trees.
+        if getattr(tree.root_node, "has_error", False):
+            continue
+
+        matches = _run_query(query, tree.root_node)
+        if not matches:
+            continue
+
+        referenced = _collect_ecmascript_references(tree.root_node)
+
+        for _pattern_idx, captures in matches:
+            import_node = _unwrap_node(captures.get("import"))
+            if not import_node:
+                continue
+
+            bindings = _extract_ecmascript_import_bindings(import_node)
+            if not bindings:
+                # Side-effect import (`import "x"`) or empty named import (`import {} from "x"`).
+                continue
+
+            line = import_node.start_point[0] + 1
+            for symbol in bindings:
+                if symbol not in referenced:
+                    entries.append({
+                        "file": filepath,
+                        "line": line,
+                        "name": symbol,
+                        "symbol": symbol,
+                    })
+
+    return entries
+
+
+def _extract_ecmascript_import_bindings(import_node) -> list[str]:
+    """Extract local binding names from an ECMAScript import_statement node."""
+    import_clause = None
+    for child in import_node.named_children:
+        if child.type == "import_clause":
+            import_clause = child
+            break
+    if import_clause is None:
+        return []
+
+    bindings: list[str] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+
+    def add(name: str | None) -> None:
+        if not name or name in seen:
+            return
+        seen.add(name)
+        bindings.append(name)
+
+    for child in import_clause.named_children:
+        # Default import: `import Foo from "x"`
+        if child.type == "identifier":
+            add(_node_text(child))
+            continue
+
+        # Namespace import: `import * as ns from "x"`
+        if child.type == "namespace_import":
+            for grand in child.named_children:
+                if grand.type == "identifier":
+                    add(_node_text(grand))
+                    break
+            continue
+
+        # Named imports: `import { a, b as c } from "x"`
+        if child.type == "named_imports":
+            for spec in child.named_children:
+                if spec.type != "import_specifier":
+                    continue
+                alias = spec.child_by_field_name("alias")
+                name = spec.child_by_field_name("name")
+                add(_node_text(alias) if alias is not None else _node_text(name))
+            continue
+
+    return bindings
+
+
+def _collect_ecmascript_references(root_node) -> set[str]:
+    """Collect identifier-like references outside ECMAScript import statements."""
+    referenced: set[str] = set()
+    stack = [root_node]
+
+    while stack:
+        node = stack.pop()
+        if node.type in _ECMASCRIPT_REFERENCE_NODE_TYPES and not _has_ancestor_type(
+            node, {_ECMASCRIPT_IMPORT_NODE_TYPE}
+        ):
+            if not _is_ecmascript_declaration_occurrence(node):
+                text = _node_text(node)
+                if text:
+                    referenced.add(text)
+
+        for child in reversed(node.named_children):
+            stack.append(child)
+
+    return referenced
+
+
+def _has_ancestor_type(node, ancestor_types: set[str]) -> bool:
+    parent = node.parent
+    while parent is not None:
+        if parent.type in ancestor_types:
+            return True
+        parent = parent.parent
+    return False
+
+
+def _is_ecmascript_declaration_occurrence(node) -> bool:
+    """Return True when `node` appears in a declaration/binding position.
+
+    This prevents counting declarations as references (e.g. destructuring patterns,
+    parameter names, catch parameters, type names).
+
+    Not a full scope resolver; it is a conservative structural filter.
+    """
+    # If we're on the right side of an assignment pattern, treat as an expression reference.
+    if _is_within_assignment_pattern_right(node):
+        return False
+
+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None:
+        # Variable declarators: `const foo = ...`, `const {a: b} = ...`
+        if cur.type == "variable_declarator":
+            name = cur.child_by_field_name("name")
+            if name is not None and _is_descendant(name, node):
+                return True
+
+        # TS/TSX params: `required_parameter` / `optional_parameter` pattern field.
+        if cur.type in ("required_parameter", "optional_parameter"):
+            pattern = cur.child_by_field_name("pattern")
+            if pattern is not None and _is_descendant(pattern, node):
+                return True
+
+        # JS params: patterns live directly under `formal_parameters`.
+        if cur.type == "formal_parameters":
+            param_root = _direct_child_under(cur, node)
+            if param_root is not None:
+                # TS/TSX wraps params in required/optional_parameter; handled above.
+                if param_root.type not in ("required_parameter", "optional_parameter"):
+                    if _is_param_binding_occurrence(param_root, node):
+                        return True
+
+        # Catch binding: `catch (e) { ... }`
+        if cur.type == "catch_clause":
+            param = cur.child_by_field_name("parameter")
+            if param is not None and _is_descendant(param, node):
+                return True
+
+        # Declaration names (function/class/type/interface/enum)
+        if cur.type in _ECMASCRIPT_DECLARATION_NAME_NODE_TYPES:
+            name = cur.child_by_field_name("name")
+            if name is not None and _is_descendant(name, node):
+                return True
+
+        # `for (const x of xs)` / `for (let x in xs)` binding.
+        if cur.type == "for_in_statement":
+            left = cur.child_by_field_name("left")
+            if left is not None and _is_descendant(left, node):
+                # Only treat as a declaration if preceded by a declaration keyword.
+                prev = left.prev_sibling
+                if prev is not None and prev.type in ("const", "let", "var"):
+                    return True
+
+        cur = cur.parent
+
+    return False
+
+
+def _is_within_assignment_pattern_right(node) -> bool:
+    """Return True if node appears within the `right` field of an assignment pattern."""
+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None:
+        parent = cur.parent
+        if parent is None:
+            return False
+        if parent.type in _ECMASCRIPT_ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN_NODE_TYPES:
+            right = parent.child_by_field_name("right")
+            if right is not None and _is_descendant(right, node):
+                return True
+        cur = parent
+    return False
+
+
+def _is_descendant(ancestor, node) -> bool:
+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None:
+        if cur == ancestor:
+            return True
+        cur = cur.parent
+    return False
+
+
+def _direct_child_under(ancestor, node):
+    """Return the direct child of `ancestor` that contains `node`, if any."""
+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None and cur.parent is not None and cur.parent != ancestor:
+        cur = cur.parent
+    if cur is not None and cur.parent == ancestor:
+        return cur
+    return None
+
+
+def _is_param_binding_occurrence(param_root, node) -> bool:
+    """Return True if `node` is part of the parameter binding pattern.
+
+    `param_root` is the direct child of `formal_parameters` that contains `node`.
+    """
+    if _is_within_assignment_pattern_right(node):
+        return False
+
+    # `x` in `(x)` or `...rest` in `(...rest)` are bindings.
+    if param_root.type in ("identifier", "rest_pattern"):
+        return True
+
+    # `x=Default` binds `x` on the left; right side is an expression.
+    if param_root.type == "assignment_pattern":
+        left = param_root.child_by_field_name("left")
+        if left is not None and _is_descendant(left, node):
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    # Destructuring patterns (object/array) bind identifiers inside them.
+    if param_root.type in ("object_pattern", "array_pattern", "pair_pattern"):

## Summary

This change improves scan performance and reduces redundant work by:

- Preserving a stable, state-backed `review_cache` dict and using it to cache expensive shared review detectors.
- Prefetching shared review detectors (boilerplate duplication + lang-specific security) so work can overlap with other phases.
- Avoiding repeat work during a scan (resolve scanned file list once; extract functions once per scan root for signature+dupes).
- Making dupes detection more incremental by caching near-duplicate pairs and recomputing only for changed functions.

## Key changes (by area)

### Scan workflow + state contract

- Normalize `state.review_cache` to a dict and pass the same reference into `LangRunOverrides` (so caches persist across scan runs).
- Resolve the scan file list once and reuse it for stale exclude auditing and codebase metrics.
- In metrics collection, resolve relative paths against the scan root and prefer in-memory `read_file_text` when available.

Files:
- `desloppify/app/commands/scan/workflow.py`
- `desloppify/app/commands/scan/helpers.py`
- `desloppify/languages/_framework/runtime_support/runtime.py`

### Shared review phases: prefetch + caching + function extraction reuse

- Add a detector-cache namespace under `review_cache["detectors"]`.
- Cache results for:
  - boilerplate duplication clusters (jscpd)
  - lang-specific security results
- Add prefetch futures (thread pool) started up-front when relevant phases are present, then consumed by the actual phase.
- Cache `lang.extract_functions(path)` once per scan root so `signature` + `dupes` don’t re-extract.
- Ensure in-memory prefetch/function caches are cleared after a scan run (including error paths).

...

> AGENT

This PR fixes a genuine re-injection bug in the workflow system. `sync_create_plan_needed()` lacked a sentinel to prevent `workflow::create-plan` from being re-added to the queue after it was already resolved within the same cycle — the existing check only looked at whether the item was currently in the queue, not whether it had already been resolved. The fix mirrors the well-established `previous_plan_start_scores` sentinel pattern already used for `sync_communicate_score_needed()`, which is the right approach.

The implementation is correct and consistent: the sentinel is set on injection, cleared at all four appropriate cycle-boundary sites, and the new `clear_create_plan_sentinel()` function is properly exported. The bulk of the diff is mechanical Black reformatting (line-length wrapping), which is fine but slightly noisy. Test numbers look solid. **Should be merged** — it's a clean, targeted fix for a real loop bug with no design concerns.

title:	Fix Rust dep graph hangs by ignoring string-literal fake imports and indexing path matches
state:	OPEN
author:	fluffypony
labels:	
assignees:	
reviewers:	
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	429
url:	https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify/pull/429
additions:	277
deletions:	36
auto-merge:	disabled
--
### Summary
This PR fixes a Rust dep-graph performance/pathology issue that could cause coupling analysis to stall or run very slowly on medium-sized codebases with complex `use` trees. On one of my codebases it ran up to 7.8gb of RAM, and ran for about 3 hours, before I killed it (M4 Max, so it's not a machine performance issue).

### Problem
Rust import extraction used a regex over comment-stripped source and could accidentally match `use ...;` text inside multiline string literals (for example large JSON/tool description strings).  
That produced giant pseudo-import specs and expensive recursive expansion work.  
On top of that, path candidate matching repeatedly scanned the full production file set in hot loops.

### Root Cause
1. `iter_use_specs` / `iter_pub_use_specs` matched imports in string content.
2. `_candidate_matches` did repeated O(N) scans in path resolution.
3. Alias/workspace metadata was repeatedly rebuilt in frequent resolution paths.

### Changes
1. In `desloppify/languages/rust/support.py`, import extraction now masks string literal content (while preserving line/offset alignment) before running import regexes, then expands matches using the original stripped text slice.
2. Added `RustProductionFileIndex` + `build_production_file_index` for absolute/relative O(1) lookup-style matching.
3. Threaded optional `production_index` through Rust resolution helpers (`resolve_use_spec`, `resolve_mod_declaration`, `resolve_barrel_targets`, `_resolve_from_source_root`, `_match_root_files`, `_candidate_matches`).
4. Updated `desloppify/languages/rust/detectors/deps.py` to build one production index per graph build and pass it through.
5. Added caching for local dependency alias index building.
6. Added regressions in `desloppify/languages/rust/tests/test_support.py`:
1. `test_iter_use_specs_ignores_use_text_inside_strings`
2. `test_match_production_candidate_uses_relative_index_key`

### Validation
1. `pytest -q desloppify/languages/rust/tests/test_support.py desloppify/languages/rust/tests/test_deps.py desloppify/languages/rust/tests/test_test_coverage.py` → `22 passed`
2. Repro against `~/Desktop/working/nsh`:
1. `build_dep_graph` (mod edges): ~5.54s
2. `build_dep_graph` (no mod edges): ~2.87s

### Impact
1. Eliminates the observed dep-graph hang/near-hang pattern from string-literal false-positive imports.
2. Reduces path resolution overhead in Rust dep graph construction.
3. Preserves existing dep-graph semantics while improving robustness and throughput.

+    )

+def _raw_string_prefix_length(chars: list[str], index: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    """Return (prefix_length, hash_count) for raw string prefixes at index."""
+    length = len(chars)
+    j = index

> AGENT

This is a solid, well-scoped PR. It replaces a naive module-path/basename heuristic for detecting unused imports in JS/TS with a proper AST binding-aware approach, correctly handling default, named, aliased, namespace, and side-effect imports — and emitting per-symbol issues rather than per-line blobs. The implementation is thorough: it handles edge cases like NUL bytes, assignment pattern defaults, parameter defaults, and type-only imports, and the 16 new tests cover all the critical paths. The only minor concern is that `_has_ancestor_type` does a parent-pointer walk which could be slow on deeply nested trees, but this is unlikely to matter in practice. Recommend merging — the false positive reduction on real OSS repos is significant, and the code is clean.

I have enough context now to give a judgement.

**Verdict: Needs work before merging.**

The PR bundles three distinct things: two legitimate bug fixes (wrong project root path for `--scan-after-import`, and `force-rescan` wiping manual clusters), plus a behavioral change (requiring explicit triage decisions for auto-clusters). The bug fixes are well-motivated and the root cause analysis in the PR description is clear. However, the manual test checklist items are all unchecked — none of the behavioral scenarios have been verified beyond the existing automated suite. Additionally, the PR mixes in unrelated additions (a `directives` command, `dev test-hermes` subcommand, a large README/CLAUDE.md rewrite, and a binary asset change), which makes it hard to review and rollback cleanly. The two bugs alone would make a clean, mergeable PR; the rest needs either its own PR or more justification that it belongs here.

> AGENT

PR #429 fixes a real and severe bug in the Rust dependency graph builder: `use` statement regexes were accidentally matching text inside multiline string literals (e.g., large JSON/tool description blobs), creating bogus pseudo-imports that caused exponential recursive expansion — leading to the reported 7.8GB RAM / 3-hour hang. The fix is sound: mask string literal contents before regex matching (preserving line offsets for accurate span extraction), add a precomputed O(1) file index to replace hot O(N) linear scans in path resolution, and cache workspace/alias index rebuilds with `lru_cache`. The approach is correct and well-tested with two regression tests. The PR is clean, well-scoped, and the validation numbers are credible.

**Verdict: merge.** This is a genuine performance pathology fix with a clear root cause, a correct and minimally invasive solution, and regression coverage. No concerns.

title:	fix(r): correct shell quote escaping in lintr command
state:	OPEN
author:	sims1253

auto-merge:	disabled
--
Bug: The R language plugin's lintr command had broken shell quote escaping that prevented it from executing properly.

   Root Cause:
   1. Quote collision: The outer Python string used single quotes, but the shell command also used single quotes for the R expression, causing the shell to receive malformed commands.
   2. Over-engineering: The cat(paste(capture.output(...), collapse="\\n")) wrapper was unnecessary — lintr::lint_dir() already prints to stdout by default.

   The Fix:

```python
     # Before (broken):
     'cmd': (
         'Rscript -e \'cat(paste(capture.output('
         'lintr::lint_dir(".", show_notifications=FALSE)'
         '), collapse="\\n"))\''
     ),

     # After (fixed):
     "cmd": (
         "Rscript -e \"lintr::lint_dir('.')\""
     ),
```
   Changes:
   •  Switched to double quotes for the Python string, allowing single quotes inside for the R string
   •  Removed unnecessary cat/paste/capture.output wrapper
   •  Simplified to rely on lintr's default stdout behavior
   •  Output remains GNU-style formatted lint messages (compatible with fmt: "gnu")
---DIFF---

+++ b/desloppify/languages/r/__init__.py
@@ -10,9 +10,7 @@

             "cmd": (
-                'Rscript -e \'cat(paste(capture.output('
-                'lintr::lint_dir(".", show_notifications=FALSE)'
-                '), collapse="\\n"))\''

   249→+
   250→+## Dependency Analysis
   251→+
   252→+### Import Resolution
   253→+
   254→+The plugin analyzes `@import` statements and resolves dependencies:
   255→+
   256→+```scss
   257→+// Direct file import - resolved to full path
   258→+@import "variables";  // → styles/_variables.scss
   259→+
   260→+// Partial import with extension
   261→+@import "mixins.scss";  // → styles/mixins.scss
   262→+
   263→+// External library import
   264→+@import "~bootstrap/scss/bootstrap";  // → node_modules/bootstrap/scss/bootstrap.scss
   265→+
   266→+// URL import (security flagged)
   267→+@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Roboto");
   268→+```
   269→+
   270→+### Dependency Graph
   271→+
   272→+```mermaid
   273→+graph TD
   274→+    A[main.scss] --> B[variables.scss]
   275→+    A --> C[mixins.scss]
   276→+    A --> D[components/_buttons.scss]
   277→+    D --> E[components/_base.scss]
   278→+    C --> F[functions/_math.scss]
   279→+```
   280→+
   281→+## Integration with Desloppify
   282→+
   283→+### Workflow Integration
   284→+
   285→+1. **Scan Phase**: Identifies SCSS files and runs initial analysis
   286→+2. **Analysis Phase**: Deep dive into code quality, security, and structure
   287→+3. **Reporting Phase**: Generates comprehensive reports with actionable insights
   288→+4. **Remediation Phase**: Provides auto-fix capabilities and guidance
   289→+
   290→+### Example Workflow
   291→+
   292→+```bash
   293→+# 1. Initial scan
   294→+desloppify scan --lang scss --path styles/
   295→+
   296→+# 2. Detailed analysis
   297→+desloppify analyze --lang scss --detailed --output analysis.json
   298→+
   299→+# 3. Generate HTML report
   300→+desloppify report --lang scss --format html --output report.html
   301→+
   302→+# 4. Apply auto-fixes
   303→+desloppify autofix --lang scss --path styles/ --dry-run
   304→+
   305→+# 5. Final verification
   306→+desloppify verify --lang scss --path styles/
   307→+```
   308→+
   309→+## Troubleshooting
   310→+
   311→+### Common Issues
   312→+
   313→+**Issue**: `stylelint not found`
   314→+**Solution**: Install stylelint globally or configure path
   315→+```bash
   316→+npm install -g stylelint
   317→+# or
   318→+desloppify config set scss.stylelint_path /path/to/stylelint
   319→+```
   320→+
   321→+**Issue**: `File too large` errors
   322→+**Solution**: Increase max file size or split large files
   323→+```yaml
   324→+# In .desloppify.scss.yml
   325→+scss:
   326→+  analysis:
   327→+    max_file_size: 20971520  # 20MB
   328→+```
   329→+
   330→+**Issue**: Timeout errors
   331→+**Solution**: Increase timeout or optimize stylelint config
   332→+```yaml
   333→+# In .desloppify.scss.yml
   334→+scss:
   335→+  stylelint:
   336→+    timeout: 60  # 60 seconds
   337→+```

## Problem

PHPStan output was silently discarded on every scan, logged as `phpstan tooling unavailable (parser_error)` then `(tool_failed_unparsed_output)`.

**Root cause 1 — `tool_runner.py`:**
Line 94 combined `stdout + stderr` before JSON parsing. PHPStan writes a diagnostic note to stderr:
```
Note: Using configuration file /path/to/phpstan.neon.dist.
```
This gets prepended to the stdout JSON, making the combined string invalid JSON → `parser_error`.

**Root cause 2 — PHP plugin `fmt='json'`:**
After fixing root cause 1, parsing still returned an empty list. The plugin declared `fmt='json'`, which routes to `parse_json()` — a flat-array parser. PHPStan outputs a nested object:
```json
{"totals": {...}, "files": {"/path/to/file.php": {"messages": [{"message": "...", "line": 42}]}}}
```
`parse_json()` expects a top-level array and returns `[]` → `tool_failed_unparsed_output`.

## Fix

1. **`tool_runner.py`**: Use `result.stdout` as the parse input when stdout is non-empty; only fall back to `stdout + stderr` for the emptiness check.

2. **`parsers.py`**: Add `parse_phpstan()` which correctly handles the nested `{"files": {path: {"messages": [...]}}}}` format. Register it in `PARSERS` as `"phpstan"`.

3. **`php/__init__.py`**: Change `fmt='json'` → `fmt='phpstan'`.

## Verification

After applying fixes, phpstan output is correctly parsed — 17 real errors from the test project are now surfaced by the detector. All 5363 existing tests pass.

+def parse_phpstan(output: str, scan_path: Path) -> list[dict]:
+    """Parse PHPStan JSON: ``{"files": {"<path>": {"messages": [{"message": "...", "line": 42}]}}}``."""
+    del scan_path
+    entries: list[dict] = []
+    data = _load_json_output(output, parser_name="phpstan")
+    files = data.get("files") if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
+    for filepath, fdata in (files or {}).items():
+        if not isinstance(fdata, dict):
+            continue
+        for msg in fdata.get("messages") or []:
+            if not isinstance(msg, dict):
+                continue
+            line = _coerce_line(msg.get("line", 0))
+            message = msg.get("message", "")
+            if filepath and message and line is not None:
+                entries.append({"file": str(filepath), "line": line, "message": str(message)})
+    return entries
+
+

   497→+# SCSS Plugin Usage Guide
   498→+
   499→+## 🎨 Overview
   500→+
   501→+The SCSS plugin provides comprehensive analysis for SCSS (Sassy CSS) files within the Desloppify code quality platform.
   502→+
   503→+**Current Status:** ✅ Fully Functional (EXCELLENT Quality 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟)
   504→+
   505→+## 🚀 Quick Start
   506→+
   507→+### Installation
   508→+The SCSS plugin is automatically included with Desloppify. Ensure you have the dependencies:
   509→+
   510→+```bash
   511→+# Install stylelint globally
   512→+npm install -g stylelint stylelint-config-standard-scss
   513→+
   514→+# Verify installation
   515→+stylelint --version  # Should show 17.x.x
   516→+```
   517→+
   518→+### Basic Usage
   519→+
   520→+```bash
   521→+# Scan a SCSS project
   522→+desloppify scan --path /path/to/scss-project --profile objective
   523→+
   524→+# View results
   525→+desloppify status
   526→+desloppify next
   527→+```
   528→+
   529→+## 🔧 Configuration
   530→+
   531→+### Stylelint Configuration
   532→+Create `.stylelintrc.json` in your project root:
   533→+
   534→+```json
   535→+{
   536→+  "extends": "stylelint-config-standard-scss",
   537→+  "rules": {
   538→+    "max-nesting-depth": 4,
   539→+    "selector-max-specificity": "0,4,0",
   540→+    "no-descending-specificity": true,
   541→+    "color-no-invalid-hex": true,
   542→+    "declaration-block-no-duplicate-properties": true
   543→+  }
   544→+}
   545→+```
   546→+
   547→+### Python API Usage
   548→+

This PR fixes a real bug in the R language plugin where broken shell quote escaping caused the lintr command to fail entirely. The fix is correct: switching to double-quoted Python strings resolves the quote collision, and dropping the `cat(paste(capture.output(...)))` wrapper is valid since `lintr::lint_dir()` already writes to stdout. The change is minimal (1 addition, 3 deletions), focused, and well-explained. **Recommend merging** — it's a straightforward bug fix with no downsides.

# PR: FrameworkSpec horizontal layer + Next.js spec (Issue #418)

Addresses #418.

## Summary
- Introduces a spec-driven **frameworks horizontal layer** (`FrameworkSpec`) with deterministic presence detection and per-framework phases.
- Migrates **Next.js** from bespoke TS/JS wiring + “primary framework” logic to a `FrameworkSpec` with **present/absent detection + evidence**.
- Integrates `next lint` as a **slow tool phase** that respects `--skip-slow` / `include_slow=False`.

## Design (per maintainer guidance)
- Scanner rules run as `DetectorPhase.run(path, lang)` with `LangRuntimeContract` — no parallel context object.
- `requires=` gates rules, and missing capabilities surface as **coverage/confidence degradation**, not silent skips.
- Framework detection is **binary** (present/absent) with evidence strings; no scoring/primary framework.
- Framework tools reuse existing tool plumbing (`make_tool_phase`) rather than adding a parallel system.

## What Changed
### Framework infrastructure
- Added framework spec contracts + registry + detection + phase factories:
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/types.py`
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/registry.py`
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/detection.py`
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/phases.py`
- Node ecosystem detection:
  - resolves nearest `package.json`
  - checks deps/devDeps/scripts/config markers
  - caches results in `lang.review_cache`

### Next.js converted to a FrameworkSpec
- `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/specs/nextjs.py`
- Runs smells + tools from the detected `package_root` (monorepo correctness).
...
</persisted-output>

> AGENT

I have enough context from the PR description, benchmarks, and diff to give a solid judgement.

This PR adds scan performance optimizations: prefetching expensive detectors (jscpd boilerplate, security) via a thread pool, caching detector results in a state-backed `review_cache` dict, resolving the file list once and reusing it across scan phases, and making near-duplicate detection incremental by caching pair results between scans. The benchmark evidence is solid — ~42% cold scan speedup on this repo, and roughly 50% on large OSS repos like Django and pandas — with full test suite passing (6166 tests).

The approach is sound and the diff is well-structured: the cache contract is properly versioned, error paths clear in-memory caches, and there's a clean `ScanStateContractError` guard on malformed state. The one notable issue is a **control flow bug** in `run_scan_generation` in `workflow.py`: the post-scan steps (`collect_codebase_metrics`, stale exclusion audit, wontfix augmentation) were moved *inside* the `try` block's body but *before* the `finally` clause — meaning those steps now run before `disable_parse_cache()`/`disable_file_cache()` are called, which is the intended order — but a quick read shows the `return` was also moved inside the `try`, which means on exception the function won't return the tuple at all. That warrants a closer look before merging.

**Verdict: needs work** — the performance gains are real and the caching design is solid, but the restructuring of the `try/finally` block in `workflow.py` introduced a logic issue where an exception before `return` will suppress the result silently rather than propagating cleanly. Worth a targeted fix-up and re-review rather than a full rework.

This is a solid, well-scoped bug fix. It correctly identifies two distinct root causes (stderr contaminating the JSON parse input in `tool_runner.py`, and the wrong parser format being used for PHPStan's nested output structure), addresses both with minimal, targeted changes, and includes thorough tests covering the new parser and the `tool_runner.py` behavior change. The `parse_input` vs `combined` separation in `tool_runner.py` is a meaningful improvement that benefits any tool (not just PHPStan) that writes diagnostic noise to stderr alongside valid JSON on stdout. Should be merged — no issues found.

**PR #428: Add SCSS language plugin**

This PR adds a new SCSS/Sass language plugin that uses the `generic_lang` framework to integrate stylelint for linting. The actual functional core — the `register()` function — is about 20 lines and is straightforward and appropriate. However, the PR is badly bloated: of the 1,233 added lines, the vast majority are two large markdown docs (`README.md`, `USAGE.md`) filled with emojis, self-congratulatory quality ratings ("EXCELLENT Quality"), placeholder URLs (`your-repo`, `discord.gg/desloppify`), and commands that don't exist in this tool (`desloppify analyze`, `desloppify report`, `desloppify verify`). The `__init__.py` also contains ~200 lines of standalone helper classes (`SCSSSecurityAnalyzer`, `SCSSMetricsCalculator`, `SCSSDependencyAnalyzer`) that are defined but never wired into the plugin — dead code. There are no tests included despite the test plan claiming they exist.

**Verdict: Needs work.** The plugin's functional core is acceptable, but the PR needs the fabricated docs removed, dead code cut, and actual tests added before it's mergeable.

> AGENT

I have enough information to give a solid judgment.

This PR introduces a `FrameworkSpec` horizontal layer — a spec-driven abstraction for framework detection and scanning, with Next.js as the first migrated framework. It's a substantial addition (3458 lines added, 20 deleted) that replaces bespoke Next.js wiring with a proper registry/detection/phase system that reuses existing tool plumbing and respects `--skip-slow`.

**Judgment:** The design is solid and follows the project's patterns well — deterministic detection, evidence-based, caches results in `lang.review_cache`, reuses `make_tool_phase` instead of inventing a parallel system. The test counts (6061 passed) are encouraging. However, this is a large surface area change for a single PR, and the mutation of `runtime_options` dict in `scan.py` (setting `include_slow`/`profile` keys directly on the lang object's dict) is a bit of a smell — it's side-effecting shared state rather than passing these as parameters. The legacy cleanup is good. Overall this is **needs work** — not because the direction is wrong, but because the `runtime_options` mutation pattern should be scrutinized, and a PR this size warrants a closer look at whether the `_framework/frameworks/` layer properly respects the project's import direction rules (base/ never importing from engine/).

# PR: FrameworkSpec horizontal layer + Next.js spec (Issue #418)

Addresses #418.

## Summary
- Introduces a spec-driven **frameworks horizontal layer** (`FrameworkSpec`) with deterministic presence detection and per-framework phases.
- Migrates **Next.js** from bespoke TS/JS wiring + “primary framework” logic to a `FrameworkSpec` with **present/absent detection + evidence**.
- Integrates `next lint` as a **slow tool phase** that respects `--skip-slow` / `include_slow=False`.

## Design (per maintainer guidance)
- Scanner rules run as `DetectorPhase.run(path, lang)` with `LangRuntimeContract` — no parallel context object.
- `requires=` gates rules, and missing capabilities surface as **coverage/confidence degradation**, not silent skips.
- Framework detection is **binary** (present/absent) with evidence strings; no scoring/primary framework.
- Framework tools reuse existing tool plumbing (`make_tool_phase`) rather than adding a parallel system.

## What Changed
### Framework infrastructure
- Added framework spec contracts + registry + detection + phase factories:
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/types.py`
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/registry.py`
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/detection.py`
  - `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/phases.py`
- Node ecosystem detection:
  - resolves nearest `package.json`
  - checks deps/devDeps/scripts/config markers
  - caches results in `lang.review_cache`

### Next.js converted to a FrameworkSpec
- `desloppify/languages/_framework/frameworks/specs/nextjs.py`
- Runs smells + tools from the detected `package_root` (monorepo correctness).
...

   279→+def _find_nearest_package_json(scan_path: Path, project_root: Path) -> Path | None:
   280→+    resolved = scan_path if scan_path.is_absolute() else (project_root / scan_path)
   281→+    resolved = resolved.resolve()
   282→+    if resolved.is_file():
   283→+        resolved = resolved.parent
   284→+
   285→+    # If scan_path is inside runtime project root, cap traversal there.
   286→+    # Otherwise (e.g. --path /tmp/other-repo), traverse from scan_path upward.
   287→+    limit_to_project_root = False
   288→+    try:
   289→+        resolved.relative_to(project_root)
   290→+        limit_to_project_root = True
   291→+    except ValueError:
   292→+        limit_to_project_root = False
   293→+
   294→+    cur = resolved
   295→+    while True:
   296→+        candidate = cur / "package.json"
   297→+        if candidate.is_file():
   298→+            return candidate
   299→+        if (limit_to_project_root and cur == project_root) or cur.parent == cur:
   300→+            break
   301→+        cur = cur.parent
   302→+
   303→+    # Fallback only when no package.json exists in the scanned tree.
   304→+    candidate = project_root / "package.json"
   305→+    return candidate if candidate.is_file() else None

   308→+def _read_package_json(package_json: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
   309→+    try:

   311→+    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   312→+        return {}
   313→+    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
   314→+

   316→+def _dep_set(payload: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> set[str]:
   317→+    deps = payload.get(key)
   318→+    if not isinstance(deps, dict):
   319→+        return set()
   320→+    return {str(k) for k in deps.keys()}
   321→+
   322→+

   324→+    scripts = payload.get("scripts")

   327→+    return [v for v in scripts.values() if isinstance(v, str)]

I have enough information to give a solid judgment.

This PR introduces a `FrameworkSpec` horizontal layer — a spec-driven abstraction for framework detection and scanning, with Next.js as the first migrated framework. It's a substantial addition (3458 lines added, 20 deleted) that replaces bespoke Next.js wiring with a proper registry/detection/phase system that reuses existing tool plumbing and respects `--skip-slow`.

**Judgment:** The design is solid and follows the project's patterns well — deterministic detection, evidence-based, caches results in `lang.review_cache`, reuses `make_tool_phase` instead of inventing a parallel system. The test counts (6061 passed) are encouraging. However, this is a large surface area change for a single PR, and the mutation of `runtime_options` dict in `scan.py` (setting `include_slow`/`profile` keys directly on the lang object's dict) is a bit of a smell — it's side-effecting shared state rather than passing these as parameters. The legacy cleanup is good. Overall this is **needs work** — not because the direction is wrong, but because the `runtime_options` mutation pattern should be scrutinized, and a PR this size warrants a closer look at whether the `_framework/frameworks/` layer properly respects the project's import direction rules (base/ never importing from engine/).

**Verdict:** This PR introduces a spec-driven `FrameworkSpec` abstraction layer for framework detection and scanning, with Next.js as the first implementation — replacing bespoke per-framework wiring with a registry/detection/phase system. The design is well-aligned with the project's existing patterns: it reuses `make_tool_phase`, caches in `review_cache`, and keeps detection deterministic and evidence-based. The main concern is the side-effecting mutation of `runtime_options` in `scan.py` to pass `include_slow`/`profile` down — this smuggles scan-time config through a mutable dict on the lang object rather than threading it as explicit parameters, which could bite later. At 3400+ lines added it's a large PR, but the structure is clean and tests pass. **Needs minor work** — fix the `runtime_options` mutation pattern, then merge.

+def _detect_unused_imports_ecmascript(
+    file_list: list[str],
+    spec: TreeSitterLangSpec,
+    parser,
+    language,
+) -> list[dict]:
+    """Binding-aware unused import detection for JavaScript/TypeScript (JSX/TSX).
+
+    Emits one entry per unused imported local binding:
+    {file, line, name, symbol}
+
+    Side-effect-only imports (e.g. `import "x"`) are ignored.
+    """
+    query = _make_query(language, f"({_ECMASCRIPT_IMPORT_NODE_TYPE}) @import")
+    entries: list[dict] = []
+
+    for filepath in file_list:
+        cached = get_or_parse_tree(filepath, parser, spec.grammar)
+        if cached is None:
+            continue
+        source, tree = cached
+
+        # Some real-world repos contain stray NUL bytes (e.g. broken fixtures).
+        # Tree-sitter can treat these as parse-stopping errors, leading to false
+        # positives due to missing references. Replace NUL with space (same length)
+        # and re-parse for analysis.
+        if b"\x00" in source:
+            source = source.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
+            tree = parser.parse(source)
+
+        # If the parse is still errorful, be conservative and skip this file to
+        # avoid false positives from incomplete trees.
+        if getattr(tree.root_node, "has_error", False):
+            continue
+
+        matches = _run_query(query, tree.root_node)
+        if not matches:
+            continue
+
+        referenced = _collect_ecmascript_references(tree.root_node)
+
+        for _pattern_idx, captures in matches:
+            import_node = _unwrap_node(captures.get("import"))
+            if not import_node:
+                continue
+
+            bindings = _extract_ecmascript_import_bindings(import_node)
+            if not bindings:
+                # Side-effect import (`import "x"`) or empty named import (`import {} from "x"`).
+                continue
+
+            line = import_node.start_point[0] + 1
+            for symbol in bindings:
+                if symbol not in referenced:
+                    entries.append({
+                        "file": filepath,
+                        "line": line,
+                        "name": symbol,
+                        "symbol": symbol,
+                    })
+
+    return entries
+
+
+def _extract_ecmascript_import_bindings(import_node) -> list[str]:
+    """Extract local binding names from an ECMAScript import_statement node."""
+    import_clause = None
+    for child in import_node.named_children:
+        if child.type == "import_clause":
+            import_clause = child
+            break
+    if import_clause is None:
+        return []
+
+    bindings: list[str] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+
+    def add(name: str | None) -> None:
+        if not name or name in seen:
+            return
+        seen.add(name)
+        bindings.append(name)
+
+    for child in import_clause.named_children:
+        # Default import: `import Foo from "x"`
+        if child.type == "identifier":
+            add(_node_text(child))
+            continue
+
+        # Namespace import: `import * as ns from "x"`
+        if child.type == "namespace_import":
+            for grand in child.named_children:
+                if grand.type == "identifier":
+                    add(_node_text(grand))
+                    break
+            continue
+
+        # Named imports: `import { a, b as c } from "x"`
+        if child.type == "named_imports":
+            for spec in child.named_children:
+                if spec.type != "import_specifier":
+                    continue
+                alias = spec.child_by_field_name("alias")
+                name = spec.child_by_field_name("name")
+                add(_node_text(alias) if alias is not None else _node_text(name))
+            continue
+
+    return bindings
+
+
+def _collect_ecmascript_references(root_node) -> set[str]:
+    """Collect identifier-like references outside ECMAScript import statements."""
+    referenced: set[str] = set()
+    stack = [root_node]
+
+    while stack:
+        node = stack.pop()
+        if node.type in _ECMASCRIPT_REFERENCE_NODE_TYPES and not _has_ancestor_type(
+            node, {_ECMASCRIPT_IMPORT_NODE_TYPE}
+        ):
+            if not _is_ecmascript_declaration_occurrence(node):
+                text = _node_text(node)
+                if text:
+                    referenced.add(text)
+
+        for child in reversed(node.named_children):
+            stack.append(child)

+    return referenced

+
+def _has_ancestor_type(node, ancestor_types: set[str]) -> bool:
+    parent = node.parent
+    while parent is not None:
+        if parent.type in ancestor_types:
+            return True
+        parent = parent.parent

+
+def _is_ecmascript_declaration_occurrence(node) -> bool:
+    """Return True when `node` appears in a declaration/binding position.
+
+    This prevents counting declarations as references (e.g. destructuring patterns,
+    parameter names, catch parameters, type names).

+    Not a full scope resolver; it is a conservative structural filter.
+    """
+    # If we're on the right side of an assignment pattern, treat as an expression reference.
+    if _is_within_assignment_pattern_right(node):

+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None:

+        if cur.type == "variable_declarator":

+            if name is not None and _is_descendant(name, node):

+        # TS/TSX params: `required_parameter` / `optional_parameter` pattern field.
+        if cur.type in ("required_parameter", "optional_parameter"):
+            pattern = cur.child_by_field_name("pattern")
+            if pattern is not None and _is_descendant(pattern, node):

+        # JS params: patterns live directly under `formal_parameters`.
+        if cur.type == "formal_parameters":

+            if param_root is not None:
+                # TS/TSX wraps params in required/optional_parameter; handled above.
+                if param_root.type not in ("required_parameter", "optional_parameter"):
+                    if _is_param_binding_occurrence(param_root, node):
+                        return True
+
+        # Catch binding: `catch (e) { ... }`
+        if cur.type == "catch_clause":
+            param = cur.child_by_field_name("parameter")
+            if param is not None and _is_descendant(param, node):
+                return True
+
+        # Declaration names (function/class/type/interface/enum)
+        if cur.type in _ECMASCRIPT_DECLARATION_NAME_NODE_TYPES:
+            name = cur.child_by_field_name("name")
+            if name is not None and _is_descendant(name, node):
+                return True
+
+        # `for (const x of xs)` / `for (let x in xs)` binding.
+        if cur.type == "for_in_statement":
+            left = cur.child_by_field_name("left")
+            if left is not None and _is_descendant(left, node):
+                # Only treat as a declaration if preceded by a declaration keyword.
+                prev = left.prev_sibling
+                if prev is not None and prev.type in ("const", "let", "var"):
+                    return True

+        cur = cur.parent
+
+    return False
+
+
+def _is_within_assignment_pattern_right(node) -> bool:
+    """Return True if node appears within the `right` field of an assignment pattern."""
+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None:
+        parent = cur.parent
+        if parent is None:
+            return False
+        if parent.type in _ECMASCRIPT_ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN_NODE_TYPES:
+            right = parent.child_by_field_name("right")
+            if right is not None and _is_descendant(right, node):
+                return True
+        cur = parent
+    return False
+
+
+def _is_descendant(ancestor, node) -> bool:
+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None:
+        if cur == ancestor:
+            return True
+        cur = cur.parent
+    return False
+
+
+def _direct_child_under(ancestor, node):
+    """Return the direct child of `ancestor` that contains `node`, if any."""
+    cur = node
+    while cur is not None and cur.parent is not None and cur.parent != ancestor:
+        cur = cur.parent
+    if cur is not None and cur.parent == ancestor:
+        return cur
+    return None
+
+
+def _is_param_binding_occurrence(param_root, node) -> bool:
+    """Return True if `node` is part of the parameter binding pattern.
+
+    `param_root` is the direct child of `formal_parameters` that contains `node`.
+    """
+    if _is_within_assignment_pattern_right(node):

+
+    # `x` in `(x)` or `...rest` in `(...rest)` are bindings.
+    if param_root.type in ("identifier", "rest_pattern"):

+
+    # `x=Default` binds `x` on the left; right side is an expression.
+    if param_root.type == "assignment_pattern":
+        left = param_root.child_by_field_name("left")
+        if left is not None and _is_descendant(left, node):
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    # Destructuring patterns (object/array) bind identifiers inside them.
+    if param_root.type in ("object_pattern", "array_pattern", "pair_pattern"):
+        return True
+
+    return False
+

440→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   441→    plan: PlanModel,
   442→    state: StateModel,
   443→    *,
   444→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   445→    current_scores: ScoreSnapshot | None = None,
   446→) -> QueueSyncResult:
   447→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` and rebaseline scores.
   448→
   449→    Injects when:
   450→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dims)
   451→    - ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue
   452→    - Score has not already been communicated this cycle
   453→      (``previous_plan_start_scores`` absent)
   454→
   455→    When injected and *current_scores* is provided, ``plan_start_scores``
   456→    is rebaselined to the current score so the score display unfreezes at
   457→    the new value.  The previous baseline is preserved in
   458→    ``previous_plan_start_scores`` so the communicate-score queue item can
   459→    show the old → new delta — and so mid-cycle scans know not to
   460→    re-inject.
   461→    """
   462→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   463→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   464→
   465→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order:
   466→        return _EMPTY()
   467→    # Already communicated this cycle — previous_plan_start_scores is set
   468→    # at injection time and cleared at cycle boundaries.
   469→    if "previous_plan_start_scores" in plan:
   470→        return _EMPTY()
   471→    if not _subjective_review_current_for_cycle(plan, state, policy=policy):
   472→        return _EMPTY()
   473→
   474→    if current_scores is not None:
   475→        _rebaseline_plan_start_scores(plan, current_scores)
   476→    # Set sentinel even when rebaseline was a no-op (no plan_start_scores
   477→    # to rebaseline) so mid-cycle scans don't re-inject.
   478→    if not plan.get("previous_plan_start_scores"):
   479→        plan["previous_plan_start_scores"] = {}
   480→    return _inject(plan, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   481→
   482→
   483→def _rebaseline_plan_start_scores(
   484→    plan: PlanModel,
   485→    scores: ScoreSnapshot,
   486→) -> None:
   487→    """Snapshot the current score as the new baseline, preserving the old one."""
   488→    old_start = plan.get("plan_start_scores")
   489→    if not isinstance(old_start, dict) or not old_start:
   490→        return
   491→    if scores.strict is None:
   492→        return
   493→
   494→    plan["previous_plan_start_scores"] = dict(old_start)
   495→    plan["plan_start_scores"] = {

1→"""Tree-sitter based unused import detection.
     2→
     3→Cross-references parsed import statements against file body to find
     4→imports whose names don't appear elsewhere in the file.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import re
    11→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    12→
    13→from .. import PARSE_INIT_ERRORS
    14→from ..imports.cache import get_or_parse_tree
    15→from .extractors import _get_parser, _make_query, _node_text, _run_query, _unwrap_node
    16→
    17→if TYPE_CHECKING:
    18→    from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import TreeSitterLangSpec
    19→
    20→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    21→
    22→
    23→def detect_unused_imports(
    24→    file_list: list[str],
    25→    spec: TreeSitterLangSpec,
    26→) -> list[dict]:
    27→    """Find imports whose names are not referenced elsewhere in the file.
    28→
    29→    Returns list of {file, line, name} entries.
    30→    """
    31→    if not spec.import_query:
    32→        return []
    33→
    34→    try:
    35→        parser, language = _get_parser(spec.grammar)
    36→    except PARSE_INIT_ERRORS as exc:
    37→        logger.debug("tree-sitter init failed: %s", exc)
    38→        return []
    39→
    40→    query = _make_query(language, spec.import_query)
    41→    entries: list[dict] = []
    42→
    43→    for filepath in file_list:
    44→        cached = get_or_parse_tree(filepath, parser, spec.grammar)
    45→        if cached is None:
    46→            continue
    47→        source, tree = cached
    48→        source_text = source.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    49→
    50→        matches = _run_query(query, tree.root_node)
    51→        if not matches:
    52→            continue
    53→
    54→        for _pattern_idx, captures in matches:
    55→            import_node = _unwrap_node(captures.get("import"))
    56→            path_node = _unwrap_node(captures.get("path"))
    57→            if not import_node or not path_node:
    58→                continue
    59→
    60→            raw_path = _node_text(path_node).strip("\"'`")
    61→            if not raw_path:
    62→                continue
    63→
    64→            # Check for alias (e.g. PHP ``use Foo as Bar``, Python ``import X as Y``).
    65→            # When an alias is present, search for the alias name instead.
    66→            alias_name = _extract_alias(import_node)
    67→
    68→            # Extract the imported name from the path.
    69→            name = alias_name or _extract_import_name(raw_path)
    70→            if not name:
    71→                continue
    72→
    73→            # Get the import statement's line range so we can exclude it
    74→            # from the search.
    75→            import_start = import_node.start_byte
    76→            import_end = import_node.end_byte
    77→
    78→            # Build text without the import statement itself.
    79→            rest = source_text[:import_start] + source_text[import_end:]
    80→
    81→            # Check if the name appears in the rest of the file.
    82→            if not re.search(r'\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\b', rest):
    83→                entries.append({
    84→                    "file": filepath,
    85→                    "line": import_node.start_point[0] + 1,
    86→                    "name": name,
    87→                })
    88→
    89→    return entries
    90→
    91→
    92→def _extract_alias(import_node) -> str | None:
    93→    """Extract alias name from import nodes.
    94→
    95→    Handles two styles:
    96→    - Go-style named imports where a ``package_identifier`` child precedes
    97→      the path with no ``as`` keyword (e.g. ``alias "pkg/path"``).
    98→    - ``as``-style aliases (Python ``import X as Y``, PHP ``use Foo as Bar``).
    99→
   100→    Returns the alias text or None.
   101→    """
   102→    # Go-style named imports: alias is a package_identifier child.
   103→    for i in range(import_node.child_count):
   104→        child = import_node.children[i]
   105→        if child.type == "package_identifier":
   106→            return _node_text(child)
   107→
   108→    # "as"-style aliases (Python, PHP, etc.)
   109→    found_as = False
   110→    for child in _iter_children(import_node):
   111→        text = _node_text(child)
   112→        if text == "as":
   113→            found_as = True
   114→            continue
   115→        # The node immediately after "as" is the alias name.
   116→        if found_as and child.type in ("name", "identifier", "namespace_name"):
   117→            return _node_text(child)
   118→    return None
   119→
   120→
   121→def _iter_children(node):
   122→    """Recursively yield terminal-ish children relevant to alias extraction.
   123→
   124→    Only descends into namespace_use_clause / import_clause nodes (the
   125→    immediate import container) — avoids descending into unrelated subtrees.
   126→    """
   127→    for i in range(node.child_count):
   128→        child = node.children[i]
   129→        # Yield leaf-like nodes (keywords, identifiers).
   130→        if child.child_count == 0:
   131→            yield child
   132→        elif child.type in (
   133→            "namespace_use_clause", "import_clause",
   134→            "namespace_alias", "as_pattern",
   135→        ):
   136→            yield from _iter_children(child)
   137→
   138→
   139→def _extract_import_name(import_path: str) -> str:
   140→    """Extract the usable name from an import path.
   141→
   142→    Examples:
   143→        "fmt" -> "fmt"
   144→        "./utils" -> "utils"
   145→        "crate::module::Foo" -> "Foo"
   146→        "com.example.MyClass" -> "MyClass"
   147→        "MyApp::Model::User" -> "User"
   148→        "Data.List" -> "List"
   149→    """
   150→    candidate = import_path.strip()
   151→    for sep in ("/", "\\"):
   152→        if sep in candidate:
   153→            parts = [p for p in candidate.split(sep) if p]
   154→            if parts:
   155→                candidate = parts[-1]
   156→
   157→    for ext in (".go", ".rs", ".rb", ".py", ".js", ".jsx", ".ts",
   158→                ".tsx", ".java", ".kt", ".cs", ".fs", ".ml",
   159→                ".ex", ".erl", ".hs", ".lua", ".zig", ".pm",
   160→                ".sh", ".pl", ".scala", ".swift", ".php",
   161→                ".dart", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".h", ".hh", ".hpp"):
   162→        if candidate.endswith(ext):
   163→            return candidate[:-len(ext)]
   164→
   165→    for sep in ("::", "."):
   166→        if sep in candidate:
   167→            parts = [p for p in candidate.split(sep) if p]
   168→            if parts:
   169→                return parts[-1]
   170→
   171→    return candidate
   172→
   173→
   174→__all__ = ["detect_unused_imports"]
   175→

1→"""Tree-sitter phase factories for language plugins.
     2→
     3→Each factory takes a ``TreeSitterLangSpec`` and returns a ``DetectorPhase``.
     4→All phases resolve ``lang.file_finder`` at runtime.
     5→
     6→Used by both generic plugins (via ``generic.py``) and full plugins (C#, Dart,
     7→GDScript, TypeScript) that want tree-sitter-powered detection without
     8→duplicating the phase construction logic.
     9→"""

    11→from __future__ import annotations

    15→
    16→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import log
    17→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import make_issue
    18→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.smell_contracts import normalize_smell_matches

    26→# ── Phase factories ────────────────────────────────────────
